transcript: Well, mind you, Noble, it's not just this. This is an example. The problem is like, at my job right now, I'm driving all the time.
output:
That makes sense. So you need something that works across the board — biking, driving, anywhere with background noise. That's exactly what a throat mic is built for. Hands free, no wind issues, voice comes through clean regardless of what's happening around you.

One thing to consider — if you're driving for work, you might want a Bluetooth version so you're not dealing with wires. Some throat mics connect via Bluetooth to your phone. The audio quality takes a small hit compared to wired, but the convenience is worth it when you're behind the wheel.

Also worth noting — if you're using this with gossamer while driving, the VAD settings might need tweaking. Engine noise and road vibration can trigger false starts. You might want a slightly higher silence threshold so it doesn't keep trying to listen when you're not talking.

Want me to help adjust those VAD settings once you get the mic set up?
